sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of default risk, and risk rises as the share of the credit limit in use goes up.
The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver, and risk generally increases with it, with the largest jump between zero and one delinquency.
The effect of utilization grows strongly with the number of delinquencies: a high utilization adds far more risk for applicants with delinquencies than for those without.
Income has a moderate effect, and risk decreases as income rises.
Length of credit history has a moderate effect, with risk decreasing as the history gets longer.
The debt-to-income ratio has a weak effect, with risk increasing as the ratio rises.
Age has negligible influence, and the data do not settle whether the number of dependents matters at all.
Recent credit inquiries and credit history length interact, with the effect of history length reversing direction depending on the number of inquiries.
